title: Kemba's March: Arizona, Then Kentucky
dek: In one week UConn beat Arizona by two in Anaheim and Kentucky by one in Houston, with both teams missing 3-pointers in the final seconds that would have won it.

facts.tip: 8:08 p.m. CT (9:08 p.m. ET), the start time on the official box score

setup.text: Three weeks earlier UConn had finished the regular season 9-9 in the Big East. It then won five games in five days at Madison Square Garden for the conference title, and two more in Washington, D.C., to reach the West Regional in Anaheim.

In the regional semifinal Kemba Walker scored 36 points against San Diego State, matching the highest-scoring NCAA tournament game in UConn history. Two nights later the opponent was fifth-seeded Arizona, which had beaten Duke 93-77 behind a career-high 32 points from Derrick Williams.

Honda Center was packed with Arizona fans, and Arizona's point guard, Lamont Jones, had been Walker's friend since the sixth grade in New York; they played two years together at Rice High School in Harlem.

The Final Four brought a rematch with Kentucky, which UConn had beaten 84-67 at the Maui Invitational in November. It also brought a family story: the father of UConn freshman Jeremy Lamb, Rolando Lamb, made the game-winning shot that knocked Jim Calhoun's Northeastern team out of the 1984 NCAA tournament. Calhoun and Kentucky's John Calipari had never hidden their dislike for each other, going back to Calipari's years at UMass.

story.text: Against Arizona, Williams picked up three fouls in the first half and played just seven minutes before the break. After his second foul UConn closed the half on a 22-7 run and led 32-25. Arizona came back, and Jesse Perry's dunk with 7:18 left put the Wildcats ahead, 53-52.

Jeremy Lamb answered with jumpers at 6:21 and 5:44, both assisted by Walker, to put UConn back in front. After an Alex Oriakhi putback, Lamb stole the ball from Williams and dunked with 3:08 left for a 62-55 lead. Walker's jumper with 1:15 to go made it 65-60.

Kyle Fogg had already hit a 3 at 1:49, and Jamelle Horne made another with 1:02 left to cut the lead to 65-63. Shabazz Napier missed a 3 with 26 seconds left. Arizona called timeout at 0:18 and got the ball to Williams at the top of the key; his deep 3 with seven seconds left was long. Fogg grabbed the rebound and passed back out to Horne, whose 3 from the right wing missed at 0:02. Lamont Jones grabbed that rebound, and time ran out, and UConn had won the West, 65-63.

In Houston, Kentucky shot 9 of 32 in the first half and trailed 31-21 at halftime, its lowest first-half total of the season. The score was tied nine times, the last at 48-48 on Doron Lamb's jumper with 7:17 left.

sequence.text: Doron Lamb's jumper, assisted by Brandon Knight, ties the game for the ninth time. It is Kentucky's last point for more than five and a half minutes.
Napier misses a layup, and Alex Oriakhi grabs the offensive rebound and scores to put UConn back in front.
Knight misses a layup, Roscoe Smith rebounds, and Walker scores on the fast break.
Napier's layup makes it a six-point game, UConn's last field goal of the night.
DeAndre Liggins steals the ball from Walker and, seconds later, hits a 3-pointer assisted by Terrence Jones. It is Kentucky's first point since the 7:17 mark.
Knight's 3 at 0:59 barely draws iron, but Josh Harrellson gets the offensive rebound. Liggins is fouled by Jeremy Lamb and makes only one of two free throws; Lamb rebounds the miss.
Knight steals the ball from Napier, and Kentucky calls timeout with a chance to win.
Kentucky goes for the win. Liggins's 3-pointer falls short, and Napier grabs the rebound.
Terrence Jones fouls Napier, a freshman, who makes both free throws.
Knight hits a 3 at the buzzer, assisted by Harrellson. It changes nothing: UConn wins 56-55 and goes to the national championship game.

quotes.text: Never did I imagine a team winning nine games in tournament play in 19 days.
When he missed it, I looked at the clock and saw zero-zero, and I just went, 'Whooooo.'
I should have drove it. It was a good shot, but it fell short.
The guys decided they didn't want to go home; this is too much fun.

aftermath.text: After the Arizona win, Walker and Calhoun hugged at center court while former UConn players Emeka Okafor and Jake Voskuhl celebrated on the floor. It was UConn's fourth Final Four, and the fourth time it had come out of the West.

The Kentucky win was UConn's 10th straight and put it in the national championship game for the third time, all under Calhoun. The Huskies ran off the court to their locker room chanting that they would shock the world.
Two nights later, on April 4, UConn beat Butler 53-41 for its third national title and 11th straight win. Walker was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player.

legacy.text: A team that had gone 9-9 in the Big East regular season won twice in one week by a total of three points to reach the title game. Both games ended with the opponent missing a 3-pointer that would have won it.
Jeremy Lamb, whose father had ended Calhoun's 1984 tournament with a last-second shot, scored 19 against Arizona and 12 against Kentucky in the two wins that sent Calhoun to his third title game.
